DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

We Drowned It Six Times

STS-HS10-L4-10001300-HSSCIENG910-BWC-LAT-01 • HS Engineering Design Grades 9-10 • Testing Design Solutions with Computer Simulations
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Isla Verde is not a real island. Marisol, Andrés, and Itzel invented it for the Build a World Challenge, and the one law of their world is that every farm has to float. They took the idea from the chinampas of Xochimilco in Mexico City, garden platforms built on a lake bed that farmers still work today, hundreds of years after the first ones were made. The team ran the storm test on the computer seven times before they put a single model in the water.
The computer says six platforms hold and four platforms fail. What else would you want the computer to test before you build the real island?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Marisol doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Marisol is doing. Give your evidence, then explain what she wants her team to conclude. Speak in three or more complete sentences.
2
What is Andrés holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Andrés is holding. Give your evidence, then explain what it lets the team find out. Speak in three or more complete sentences.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what the teacher is doing. Give your evidence, then explain what his action puts to the test. Speak in three or more complete sentences.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what place this is. Give your evidence, then explain why the team chose it for this work. Speak in three or more complete sentences.
5
Tell me about the water tank.
Look at the picture. Justify what is inside the tank. Give your evidence, then explain what the team learns from it. Speak in three or more complete sentences.
6
What is Itzel wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Itzel has on. Give your evidence, then explain how that detail keeps a listener from confusing her with someone else. Speak in three or more complete sentences.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: NGSS HS-ETS1-4 — Use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions on a complex system. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
